short_description: Consumer-facing physical trait that reports a cautious panel-relative signal related to body mass index tendency within the current local reference panel.
summary_note: Usable consumer-facing physical trait with strong raw-array support and a clearer interpretation boundary between inherited BMI-related tendency and real-world measured body size for the no-imputation workflow.
what_it_measures: A panel-relative polygenic signal associated with body mass index tendency, calibrated within the current local empirical reference panel.
interpretation_template: BMI tendency is presented here as a cautious panel-relative signal, not as a direct readout of your current measured BMI or as a diagnosis of metabolic health. {interpretation}
caution_text: Use as a cautious panel-relative signal only. No imputation or ancestry-adjusted normalization is used, and the output should not be treated as a deterministic real-world result, a direct estimate of current BMI, or medical guidance.
limitations: Percentiles and z-scores are relative to the local reference panel, not to a population-wide benchmark.

Real-world BMI is influenced strongly by diet, physical activity, age, medication use, illness, socioeconomic context, and other non-modeled factors, so this should not be treated as a precise prediction of current body size or health status.
BMI itself is an imperfect body-size proxy and does not directly distinguish fat mass, muscle mass, or body-fat distribution.
confidence_note: Confidence reflects overlap and reference robustness under the no-imputation raw-array workflow, not certainty about the real-world trait.
reference_note: Percentiles and z-scores are calibrated against a local empirical reference artifact built from raw-array files in this project; they are panel-relative, not population-wide.
